title: Rodent model of disuse-induced bone loss by hind limb injection with botulinum toxin A
author: Brent, Lodberg, et al.

steps.title: Induce General Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal with 3 % isoflurane by inhalation and confirm deep anesthesia (no response to external pain stimuli) before proceeding.

steps.title: Shave Right Hind Limb
steps.instruction: Use an electric shaver to remove all fur from the right hind limb.

steps.title: Disinfect Hind Limb
steps.instruction: Apply 70 % alcohol to the shaved area and allow it to air‑dry completely.

steps.title: Prepare Diluted BTX Solution and Load Syringe
steps.instruction:
Dilute botulinum toxin type A (Botox or equivalent) with sterile 0.9 % NaCl saline to a final concentration of 20 IU ml⁻¹. Add 2.5 ml saline to a 50 IU vial or 5 ml saline to a 100 IU vial. Calculate the required dose: 2 IU per 100 g body weight for mice; 4 IU total for rats (≥12 weeks old). 
• For rats: withdraw the calculated volume (0.2 ml for a 4 IU dose) into a 1 ml syringe, attach a 25 G needle, tap gently to remove air bubbles, and depress the plunger until the correct volume is in the needle.
• For mice: use a 50 µl Hamilton syringe with a 25 G needle. Fill the syringe from the open end, insert the plunger, and depress until the required volume is present. 
For mice, determine the total diluted BTX volume (µl) at 20 IU ml⁻¹ using the following table (body weight g → volume µl): 15 → 151, 16 → 161, 17 → 171, 18 → 181, 19 → 191, 20 → 201, 21 → 211, 22 → 221, 23 → 231, 24 → 241, 25 → 251, 26 → 261, 27 → 271, 28 → 281, 29 → 291, 30 → 301.

substeps.instruction: Load 50 µl Hamilton syringe for mice

steps.title: Inject BTX into Rat Hind Limb
steps.instruction:
Using the 1 ml syringe, inject a total of 4 IU BTX into the right hind limb as follows: 
1. Quadriceps femoris – 2 IU split into two injections (¼ ml volume each): proximal and distal. Grip the muscle, insert the needle at a 45° angle with the tip pointing proximally toward the femoral bone. Advance until the tip contacts bone, then withdraw slowly while injecting 0.05 ml.
2. Hamstring muscles – 1 IU (0.05 ml). Grip, insert needle perpendicular to the femur, advance to bone contact, withdraw slowly while injecting 0.05 ml.
3. Calf muscles – 1 IU (0.05 ml). Grip, insert needle perpendicular to the tibia, advance to bone contact, withdraw slowly while injecting 0.05 ml.

steps.title: Inject BTX into Mouse Hind Limb
steps.instruction:
Using the 50 µl Hamilton syringe, inject the calculated total volume (see table) as follows: 
1. Quadriceps femoris – inject half of the total volume into the middle part of the muscle. Grip the muscle, insert the needle perpendicular to the femur, advance until bone contact, then withdraw slowly while delivering the half‑volume.
2. Calf muscles – inject the remaining half of the total volume using the same technique (perpendicular insertion into the middle of the calf, bone contact, slow withdrawal while injecting).

steps.title: Allow Animal Recovery
steps.instruction: Place the animal in an empty housing container, monitor until it regains normal gait and limb function (typically evident one day after injection).

steps.title: Neutralize and Dispose BTX Vial
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 % hypochlorite solution to the BTX vial to neutralize the toxin, then discard the vial as hazardous waste.

steps.title: Dispose Contaminated Syringes
steps.instruction: Discard all single‑use syringes that have contacted BTX as hazardous waste.

steps.title: Decontaminate Reusable Syringe
steps.instruction: Fill the Hamilton syringe with 0.5 % hypochlorite, place it horizontally for 5 min. Submerge the plunger in the same solution for 5 min.

steps.title: Clean and Store Syringe
steps.instruction: Rinse the syringe and plunger with sterile water, then with acetone. Allow them to dry completely before storing for later use.
